name: Pay suppliers and carriers
summary: Accounts payable clerks receive supplier and carrier invoices, check each one against the purchase order and goods receipt, or for sand hauling against the load tickets, get non-PO invoices approved, post them and pay them in weekly EFT runs when they fall due. Most of the effort goes into exceptions: price and quantity differences that buyers must settle, missing receipts, and carrier statements whose loads do not match the logistics team's tickets. Payments are released only after the controller and treasury approve the run.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company buying sand, trucking, chemicals, cement, fuel, gases and parts from a few hundred suppliers, with a ten-person accounts payable team in Calgary paying through an ERP with OCR scanning and weekly EFT runs.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: an ERP with billing, AR and AP modules, tablet field ticketing linked to the price book, customer e-invoicing networks (mainly OpenInvoice), OCR scanning of supplier invoices, email, phone and Excel. No machine-learning coding or matching.

trigger: A supplier or carrier invoice arrives by email, the supplier network or post.
end_state: The invoice is paid by EFT or cheque and posted, or is rejected as a duplicate.

volume.seasonality: Follows field activity with a two- to four-week lag: highest from February to April, lowest in June, with a second rise in the fall. Sand and trucking invoices swing most.

evidence.note: Q4 2022 direct costs were $133.4 million (trican-mda-2022), mostly supplier spend; at an assumed average invoice of $8,000-12,000 that is about 4,000-5,500 invoices a month in a busy quarter. Matches the organisation file's demand driver.

surge.cause: Year-end and Q1 invoice wave as producers close capital programs and winter work peaks

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's surge for this process.

About 20 minutes of hands-on time per invoice on average over about 4,500 invoices a month is about 11 FTE at 130 productive hours, more than the ten clerks can give; in practice clerks work overtime at month end and the winter peak, and the long tail of exceptions is worked in batches.
Settles PO price and quantity exceptions, about 20 minutes each on about 700 a month including re-matches.
Confirms disputed sand haul loads, about 30 minutes each on about 380 carrier invoices a month.
Approves non-PO invoices for base and field costs, a few minutes each.
Sets up and verifies new supplier records, kept apart from AP clerks.
Second approval above delegation limits and review of the weekly payment run.
Second release of the EFT file in the bank portal.

systems.name: ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Customer e-invoicing and field ticket approval networks
Invoice scanning and OCR capture into the ERP

steps.name: Scan and capture the invoice
steps.description: Invoices emailed to the AP mailbox or received on paper are scanned and read by OCR into the ERP's invoice inbox with supplier, invoice number, date, amount, GST and PO number; invoices from supplier networks arrive as data. The batch runs several times a day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Index the invoice and check for duplicates
steps.description: The AP clerk confirms the OCR fields against the image, corrects misread amounts or PO numbers, checks the supplier's GST number and searches for the same invoice number and amount already entered. She routes the invoice by type: PO, carrier haul statement or non-PO.

error.defect_description: Amount or PO number misread and not corrected.

next.condition: carrier haul invoice with load tickets
new supplier not yet set up

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: ERP three-way match
steps.description: The ERP compares the invoice with the purchase order price and the goods receipt quantity, within set tolerances. Matched invoices go straight to posting; differences go to the clerk's exception queue.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: three-way match of PO, receipt and invoice before payment

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Investigate the match exception
steps.description: The clerk opens the PO, receipt and invoice side by side and works out whether the price, the quantity or a missing receipt is the problem, then emails the buyer or the warehouse with the details.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Buyer resolves the price or quantity difference
steps.description: The procurement specialist checks the agreed price and the delivery with the supplier and the warehouse, then amends the PO, has the receipt posted, or asks the supplier for a credit or corrected invoice.
outputs: amended PO, receipt or credit request

next.condition: supplier must send a credit or corrected invoice

evidence.note: APQC median exception rate about 5% cross-industry (corpay-ap-benchmarks); oilfield parts and chemicals with frequent price changes run higher. Shares and times tier C.

steps.name: Match the carrier invoice to load tickets
steps.description: For sand hauling and other carrier invoices the clerk compares each load on the statement with the logistics team's load tickets and bills of lading: date, truck, origin terminal, well site, weight and standby hours, using the logistics spreadsheet or report. Lines without a ticket or with extra standby are flagged.

error.defect_description: A load billed twice across two statements is not caught.

evidence.note: Each sand container or load carries a bill of lading that is verified and sent to payables; around 200 container loads a day on a busy pad (aogr-proppant-2018). Times tier C.

steps.name: Logistics coordinator confirms disputed loads
steps.description: The proppant logistics coordinator checks the disputed loads against dispatch records, telematics and wellsite delivery confirmations, talks to the carrier's dispatcher and approves or rejects each line.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Code haul charges to the job
steps.description: The clerk codes each approved haul line to the job and well so that billing can rebill pass-through hauling to the customer, and attaches the load tickets.

error.defect_description: Haul charged to the wrong well.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Code the non-PO invoice and route it
steps.description: For rentals, services, utilities and other non-PO invoices the clerk enters the GL account, cost centre and job if known, and routes the invoice in the ERP workflow to the budget holder named by the supplier or the district.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Budget holder approves the non-PO invoice
steps.description: The district manager (or the relevant shop or department manager) checks that the service was received and the cost is his, and approves, corrects the coding, or rejects it. Field managers approve in batches when they are in the office.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: non-PO spend approved by the budget holder

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Controller gives second approval
steps.description: Invoices above the budget holder's limit go to the controller, who checks the contract or quote behind the charge before approving.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: invoices above set limits approved by the corporate controller

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Post the invoice
steps.description: The clerk posts the matched or approved invoice in the ERP, which records the liability and the due date from the supplier's payment terms.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Hold for the payment run on the due date
steps.description: The posted invoice waits until its due date, then the ERP picks it up in the weekly payment proposal. Most suppliers are paid on 30-day terms counted from the invoice date, some later.

evidence.note: Trade and other payables of $90.9 million at year-end 2022 against Q4 direct costs of $133.4 million (trican-mda-2022) is about two months, but payables include accrued payroll and capital items; supplier terms of about 30-45 days from invoice date are assumed.

steps.name: Controller reviews the payment run
steps.description: The controller reviews the weekly payment proposal for large or unusual payments, new or changed bank details and cash position, removes items to hold, and approves the run.

control.basis: Payment runs prepared by AP and approved by the controller; AP cannot release payments

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for the supplier's credit or corrected invoice
steps.description: The supplier or carrier is asked for a credit memo or a corrected invoice and sends it when their billing team gets to it; the original is held.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Send the EFT file and remittance
steps.description: The ERP creates the EFT file for the bank and emails remittance advices to suppliers; cheques are printed for the few suppliers without banking details.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Answer the supplier's payment inquiry
steps.description: A supplier or carrier calls or emails asking when an invoice will be paid; the clerk looks up its status, due date and any hold and replies, or asks the supplier to resend an invoice AP never received.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Treasury releases the bank file
steps.description: The treasury manager logs into the bank portal and gives the second release of the EFT file after checking the total against the approved run and the cash forecast.

control.basis: Dual authorisation of bank payments: a second signer releases the EFT file

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Set up and verify the new supplier
steps.description: An accountant outside AP sets up the new supplier from its vendor form, checks the GST registration and confirms the bank details by calling a known contact before payment can be made.

control.basis: Vendor master changes made and verified outside accounts payable to prevent payment fraud

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: PO match exception
exceptions.description: Price, quantity or missing receipt on a PO invoice; the buyer fixes the PO or receipt, or asks the supplier for a credit.

exceptions.name: Disputed haul loads
exceptions.description: Carrier statement lines with no load ticket or disputed standby; logistics confirms or rejects them.

exceptions.name: Supplier credit or reissue
exceptions.description: The supplier or carrier must send a credit memo or corrected invoice before payment.

exceptions.name: Non-PO approval delay
exceptions.description: Non-PO invoices wait for field managers to approve them between trips to the field.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from invoice receipt to payment

evidence.note: Estimate. Paying on terms of about 30-45 days from the invoice date with weekly runs; payables of about two months of direct costs at year-end 2022 (trican-mda-2022) include accruals. Cross-industry APQC median of 15 days receipt to payment (corpay-ap-benchmarks) measures processing, not payment on terms.

benchmarks.population: APQC Open Standards Benchmarking, cross-industry (as reported by Corpay, 2026)

evidence.note: Secondary report of an APQC figure; period not stated.

benchmarks.population: APQC, reported via CFO.com and Corpay

evidence.note: The organisation's 10 AP clerks on $560-870 million revenue is about 11-18 per $1 billion, between the two.

pain_points.description: Carrier statements cover many loads that must be matched one by one to load tickets held by the logistics team, and missing tickets or standby disputes need the coordinator's time.

evidence.note: High load counts and ticket data per load on frac sand deliveries.

pain_points.description: PO price and quantity exceptions wait in buyers' queues while suppliers call about payment.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Non-PO invoices wait for field managers who approve in batches between field trips.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: OCR misreads and duplicate submissions from suppliers who email and post the same invoice need manual checks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: A job is typically represented by an invoice and invoice frequency depends on how often the customer asks to be billed during a project; 7,625 jobs in 2022 and 7,291 in 2021; Q4 2022 revenue $236.5 million and Q4 2021 $156.4 million; trade and other receivables $175.4 million at December 31, 2022 and $127.8 million at December 31, 2021; trade and other payables $90.9 million at December 31, 2022; Q4 2022 direct costs $133.4 million; more than 60 customers; one customer 40% of accounts receivable in 2022 (35% in 2021) and 31% of revenue; expected credit losses measured with a provision matrix; working capital and credit facilities cover timing differences between cash collections and payments.

sources.title: AP Team Productivity: Benchmarks and How Automation Moves Them
sources.supports: Table attributed to APQC Open Standards Benchmarking: cost per invoice $6.00 median; invoice cycle time 15 days median from receipt to payment; about 5% exception rate (95% of disbursements error-free the first time); APQC work reported via CFO.com: top performers 6.2 or fewer AP FTEs per $1 billion of revenue, bottom performers 21.6 or more. Cross-industry figures reported by a payments vendor in 2026.

sources.title: Real-Time Data Collection Optimizes Proppant Logistics
sources.supports: August 2018: container sand delivery adds work for frac van personnel recording delivery tickets; about 200 containers a day on a wellsite; bill of lading data tied to each container and stage and sent electronically for verification and billing to payables.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The OCR capture tool is added as a workflow system (ocr-capture); the organisation file has no separate system for it.
District managers (non-PO approvers), an accountant (supplier master) and the treasury manager (second payment release) are added; they are in the organisation file but not listed for this process.
Average invoice of about $8,000-12,000 is an estimate used to check the organisation file's 4,500 invoices a month against direct costs.

The wait for the due date (s13) dominates the cycle time and depends on negotiated terms; the APQC 15-day median is a processing benchmark for companies that measure receipt to payment and is not comparable to paying on terms.
Invoices for sand bought by customers directly are not handled here.
The simulated median (about 24 days, p90 about 34) is below the 30-day estimate; the difference is in the assumed payment terms at s13 and is within the range of terms suppliers were paid on.

Hands-on time implies about 12 AP clerk FTE against the organisation file's 10 clerks; either the clerks ran at bottom-quartile productivity with overtime, or step times here are slightly high. 4,500 invoices a month by 10 clerks is about 5,400 invoices per clerk a year.
Matched and approved PO invoices take no human approval beyond the three-way match, as is common in ERP-based AP in 2019-2022.
